days.why: A marriage, a sister who saw the daffodils first, a mother and daughter sitting together.
days.cross_text: He went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God's Kingdom. With him were the twelve, and certain women … Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod's steward; Susanna; and many others who served them from their possessions.

days.orthodox: Venerable Paraskevi of Serbia; St Cosmas the Hymnographer
days.spine: Letter 8: we are not alone in sadness
days.why: A hymn that rides the storm, a promise not to be overcome, a steamer in a gale.
days.cross_text: He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Being afraid, they marveled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

days.orthodox: Venerable Euthymius the New; Hieromartyr Lucian of Antioch
days.spine: Letter 4 (Worpswede, 16 Jul 1903): love the questions
days.why: The God who is beside you, the ladder of beauty, a philosopher searching with a lamp.
days.cross_text: Herod said, “I beheaded John, but who is this about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.

days.orthodox: Martyr Longinus the Centurion; St Gall
days.spine: Letter 1: no poor, indifferent place
days.why: A little house that is enough, a small pudding nobody calls small, a lunch in the wheat.
days.cross_text: “You give them something to eat.” … They ate and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

days.orthodox: Prophet Hosea; Martyr Andrew of Crete; Saints Cosmas and Damian
days.spine: Letter 10: art too is only a way of living
days.why: One who holds the falling, a woman's hand on a crab tree, a hand making Adam and Eve.
days.cross_text: “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.

days.orthodox: Holy Apostle and Evangelist Luke (20th Sunday after Pentecost)
days.spine: Letter 10: a way of living
days.why: The child as father of the man, the secret of mirth, Luke the painter at his easel.
days.cross_text: In that same hour, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, “I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children.”
